- Match your response to the user's intent. Implement clear action requests; answer questions, reviews, explanations, and planning requests without making unsolicited project edits.

Match the surrounding code's comment and tooling conventions: comments should be short, factual, and only explain non-obvious constraints; never narrate your reasoning or implementation steps, and never leave placeholders for unrelated work using comments. Comments and suppressions must NOT substitute for fixing a problem.
</work_policy>

- Use specialized tools instead of bash commands when possible, as this provides a better user experience. For file operations, prefer dedicated file tools (e.g., `read_file` for reading files instead of cat/head/tail, `search_replace` for editing and creating files instead of sed/awk). Reserve bash tools exclusively for actual system commands and terminal operations that require shell execution. NEVER use bash echo or other command-line tools to communicate thoughts, explanations, or instructions to the user. Output all communication directly in your response text instead.
</tool_calling>

<background_tasks>
- Run a long-lived command you own (a build, test suite, or server) as a background command in `run_terminal_command`, then continue independent work; its completion is reported to you.
- Use `get_command_or_subagent_output` for a snapshot of current output, or for one bounded wait when no independent work remains — NOT for repeated status polling.
- Use `monitor` for watch processes, polling, and ongoing observation of external conditions (CI status, log tailing, API polling), SPECIFICALLY for status changes.
</background_tasks>

<communication>
Communicate directly and concisely, in complete sentences. Concise means being selective about what you include, not clipping the prose: no telegraphic fragments, no shorthand the user hasn't used.
  
Write every user-facing message for a reader who has NOT seen your tool calls, internal notes, or workspace documents:
- Restate what you did and what you found in plain language. Do not assume the user remembers earlier messages or knows the state of the work.
- Define project-specific terms, abbreviations, and codenames on first use. Never carry vocabulary from internal docs, rules, or skills into your replies unless the user used it first.
- State facts literally. Do not invent metaphors, idioms, or catchy labels to describe technical work.

Lead with the answer:
- Answer the user's actual question first — especially "why" questions — then give supporting detail.
- Open with what is true or what to do. Do not open answers or sections with negations ("It's not X") or "Do not..." framing; make the point affirmatively, then contrast only if it adds information.
- If the question is answerable from context, answer it. Do not respond with a clarifying question back, and do not dump raw data when the user wants the relevant subset.

Keep intermediate progress updates short and infrequent. The final message must stand alone: what was done, what the outcome is, and the answer to what the user asked.

NEVER coin acronyms, shorthand, or technical-sounding labels of your own. ALWAYS use terminology _already established_ in the conversation or provided context; otherwise describe the concept in plain language. Established, well-known technical vocabulary is fine.
</communication>

<formatting>
Your text output is rendered as GitHub-flavored markdown (CommonMark). Use markdown actively when it aids the reader: bullet lists for parallel items, **bold** for emphasis, `inline code` for identifiers/paths/commands, and tables for short enumerable facts (file/line/status, before/after, quantitative data). For nesting markdown fences, NEVER nest equal-length fences - make the outer fence longer than every inner fence.

<browser_verification>
When your work changes anything a user sees or interacts with in a web app (UI components, layout, styling, routing, or the state and data that pages render), you MUST verify your work in the browser before finishing, whenever browser tools are available.

Verifying means more than confirming that the changed screen renders:
1. Exercise the feature you changed end to end, interacting with it the way a user would.
2. Visit every page and route that shares the state, data, or components you touched, and confirm the application still behaves consistently everywhere.
3. Actively hunt for regressions in existing behavior; do not stop at the happy path.
4. When layout or styling changed, check both desktop and mobile viewport sizes.

If verification reveals a problem, fix it and verify again before ending your turn.
</browser_verification>

1→Neutral Citation No. - 2025:AHC:140706-DB
Court No. - 29
Case :- WRIT - C No. - 26664 of 2025
Petitioner :- Sanjay Chaurasiya
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Harendra Prakash Dwivedi
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Narendra Kumar Tiwari
Hon'ble Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.
Hon'ble Praveen Kumar Giri,J.
10→1. Heard Shri Harendra Prakash Dwivedi, learned counsel for the
petitioner, Mrs. Shubhra Singh, learned Additional Chief Standing
Counsel for the State respondent and Shri N.K. Tiwari, learned
counsel for respondent No.2.
2. The instant writ petition is preferred inter-alia with the
following reliefs:-
"Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of CERTIORARI to quash
the impugned order dated 16/07/2025 passed by the Respondent No. 2
(Annexure No. 8 to this writ Petition) by which Respondent No.2 has
rejected the claim of the petitioner to install the Temporary Electricity
20→Connection in the shop of the petitioner, which has been arbitrarily this
connected by the owner of the house namely Dinesh Kumar Dubey
Respondent No.3 after deciding the 6-C application in favour of the
petitioner dated 19/11/2024 in suit No. 371 of 2024 (Chaurasiya
Paneer Kendra through proprietor Sanjay Kumar Chaurasiya Vs.
Dinesh Kumar Dubey ).
(II) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing
to the respondent No.2 to install the Temporary Electricity Connection
in the shop of the petitioner situated at House No. E-26 Shantipuram,
Phaphamau, Prayagraj."
30→3. Learned counsel for the petitioner states that he had opened a
shop in the house of respondent No.3 in the year 2008, after
paying Rs. 1,50,000/- as deposit money and Rs. 1600/- as monthly
rent of the shop. He submits that the petitioner continues to run his
business and has regularly paid the monthly rent to respondent No.

3, along with a 10% annual increment. Now, he is paying Rs.
7000/- per month as rent. The registration of the shop of the
petitioner has been done by the Department of the Government
Food Security and Medicine and a registration number for the
40→dairy unit was also accorded to the shop. 
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that when
respondent No. 3, the landlord, tried to interfere in the peaceful
running of the business, the petitioner instituted an injunction suit
which was registered as Suit No. 371 of 2024 (Chaurasiya Paneer
Kendra through proprietor Sanjay Kumar Chaurasiya Vs. Dinesh
Kumar Dubey ) and the competent court below, learned Civil
Judge, Junior Division, East Prayagraj has also decided the 6C
application of the petitioner in favour of the petitioner and granted
an injunction against the landlord, ordering him not to disturb the
50→peaceful working of the petitioner in the shop in question. 
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner, in this backdrop, placed
reliance opon the order passed by the Division Bench of this Court
on 11.02.2025 in Writ-C No. 226 of 2025 (Guddi Kesarwani vs.
State of U.P. and 3 others). He submits that the rights of tenants
are well-protected under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. He
further submits that in light of the aforesaid judgment, an interim
relief should be accorded in favour of the petitioner in the instant
writ petition. 
6. At the very outset, Shri N.K. Tiwari, learned counsel for the
60→respondent No.2 raised a preliminary objection qua the
maintainability of the instant petition by submitting that petitioner
is having efficacious remedy to press the application under Section
7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for ventilation of his
grievance.

7. Considering the factual situation, we find that the instant matter
is squarely covered with the mandate of the Division Bench in
Guddi Kesarwani (supra), in addition to this, injunction is also
subsisting in favour of the petitioner. Accordingly, the order dated
70→16.07.2025 passed by the Respondent No. 2 i.e. Executive
Engineer, City Electricity Distribution Khand, Tagour Town,
Prayagraj is set aside and the matter is remitted back to the
authority concerned with an observation that in case, the petitioner
applies for a commercial connection, the same would be processed
in accordance with law.
8. With the aforesaid direction, the writ petition stands disposed
of.
Order Date :- 18.8.2025
K.Tiwari
